newsitem.title: USA: Muni bond dealers warn Senate panel on de minimis.
newsitem.headline: Muni bond dealers warn Senate panel on de minimis.

text.p: Municipal bond dealers on Thursday continued to press congressional tax committees to reject the Clinton Administration plan to repeal the two percent "de minimis" rule.

PSA The Bond Market Trade Association submitted written testimony to the Senate Finance Committee warning that de minimis repeal would raise the cost of capital for municipalities, discourage job creation and weaken the overall economy.
Currently, the Internal Revenue Service does not permit businesses to deduct interest on debt that they use to finance the purchase of tax-exempt bonds.

However, the IRS said in 1972, in what is dubbed the de minimis rule, that it will not monitor whether a corporation has borrowed to purchase tax-exempt bonds as long as those holdings total less than two percent of a firm's net assets.

Last month, thirty-five top executives from banks and securities firms urged Rep. Bill Archer, R-Texas, chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, to reject Clinton's proposal. They said the plan would have a "severe negative effect on investment in the municipal bond market."
